newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI mines lift Dec qtr after tax profit.
newsitem.headline: JCI mines lift Dec qtr after tax profit.

text.p: South African mining house JCI Ltd's three gold mines lifted after tax profit for the three months to end-December by almost four percent to 132.89 million rand from 128.24 million in the previous quarter.
JCI said on Tuesday that the company's results were boosted by increased gold output and a higher rand gold price received.
"The above was a consequence of an increase in both gold production and gold price received... coupled with a 7.8 percent increase in total working costs," JCI said.

Gold production increased by 6.1 percent to 11,724 kg from 11,049 kg in the September quarter while the average gold price increased by 2.0 percent to 56,096 rand/kg from 54,982 rand/kg in the previous quarter.
JCI said the average yield increased to 4.26 g/t from the 4.07 g/t while tonnes milled increased to 2,754,000 tonnes from 2,713,000.

Capital expenditure for the three mines, Randfontein Estates Gold Mining Co Witwatersrand Ltd, Western Areas Gold Mining Company Ltd and HJ Joel Gold Mining Co Ltd, increased to 160.66 million rand from the 126.21 million in the three months to September.
Average unit costs for the mines increased to 47,726 rand/kg from 46,961 kg.
Randfontein was the star performer, lifting net profit to 43.83 million rand from 37.44 million.

JCI's gold and uranium division chief executive John Brownrigg said at a results presentation that Western Areas' gold production of 4,832 kg was the highest reported at the mine since September 1980.
And Joel's production of 1,792 kg was the highest ever at the mine, he added.

Joel reported a 7.9 percent increase in working costs to 39,712 rand/kg from 36,805 rand/kg in the September quarter but Brownrigg said JCI still aimed at making the mine one of the lowest cost producers in the South African gold mining industry.
"We are still determined to place the company at the bottom end of the cost curve of South African producers," he said.
JCI said Joel's tonnage milled, gold production and cash flow were all positive when compared to forecasts issued in March 1996.

"Full calendar operations are in place generating significant benefits for both company and employees with current levels of production expected to be maintained during the coming quarter," the company said.
